name: Greater Israel
summary: Greater Israel is the nationalist and religious claim that the Jewish people hold an eternal right to the whole Land of Israel, at minimum the territory between the Mediterranean and the Jordan plus the Golan, and in wider versions land east of the Jordan or beyond. Its carriers keep that territory under Israeli sovereignty, refuse to trade land for peace, and treat Jewish settlement as the central Zionist task. Religious adherents add that holding the land belongs to redemption, while secular Revisionists argue from security and national right.
scope: The narrow, mainstream variant as held by the Israeli right today and at its peak after 1967: the Likud platform of 1977, the Revisionist tradition of Jabotinsky and Begin, the 1967 Movement for Greater Israel and Gush Emunim religious settlers. It excludes the maximal Nile-to-Euphrates readings and Kach-style transfer programmes, which are minority strands. Economic and social questions are mostly outside the doctrine, so most answers there are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Greater Israel is a territorial doctrine with no health-care position; adherent parties span Likud free-marketeers and religious parties backing the welfare state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Territorial claim, not economic policy; the Likud, religious-Zionist and former Labor strands that held it split on wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The doctrine says nothing on markets; Movement for Greater Israel members came from both Labor and Revisionist camps.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1967 movement included Labor kibbutz figures, but its modern carriers (Likud, settler right) lean toward privatisation; inferred only.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No stated tax position; adherents ranged from Tabenkin's Labor left to Likud's right, so genuinely split.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed; the movement united ex-Histadrut Labor figures with Revisionists who were hostile to the Histadrut.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Likud platform defends settlement land claims on national not property-rights grounds; no general property doctrine.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Outside the doctrine's concerns; no sourced position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; religious-Zionist adherents defend welfare while Likud leaders have cut it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative ownership is a Labor-Zionist theme, but the modern carriers of the idea mostly reject it; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Likud platform treats the PLO as assassins to be eliminated, implying a security-first view of terror; surveillance itself is not discussed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; the religious and nationalist right that carries the idea is generally prohibitionist.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the nationalist right typically resists speech restrictions, inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The doctrine is not about executive power; adherents defend Knesset and court systems while criticising judicial gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: The doctrine demands Israeli state sovereignty over all land between the sea and the Jordan, so it is intensely statist.

limit-guns.rationale: Settler movements favour armed civilian defence; gun policy is not stated, so inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Holding and defending the territories rests on military control; the Likud platform stresses security and eliminating terror organisations.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Religious-Zionist strand is morally conservative; no stated position.

decide-locally.rationale: The platform puts sovereignty with the central Israeli state over the entire territory.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; no source on penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: Religious-Zionist adherents hold traditional family values, but it is not part of the territorial doctrine.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Gush Emunim and Hardal religious strands oppose it; secular Likud adherents are split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Religious strand opposes it, secular Likud voters are mixed; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religious Zionists tie the land to redemption and want a Jewish public character; secular Revisionists are split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; adherents generally reject remedial identity politics.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Religious strand rejects it; no direct source.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Jewish national revival and settlement as the focal point of the Zionist effort is central to the platform.

gradual-change.rationale: Gush Emunim created facts on the ground quickly through settlement rather than waiting on institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Aliyah of diaspora Jews is encouraged; non-Jewish immigration is not discussed, so inferred toward restriction while opposing reduction of Jewish immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The 1977 platform rejects any solution formula imposed from outside, and the idea is defined against international partition claims.

free-trade.rationale: The doctrine has no trade position, and its adherents range from protectionist to free-market.

nation-first.rationale: The platform subordinates diplomacy to Israel's sovereignty claim and security; peace talks must not trade away the land.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would split between security-based and universalist reasons.

open-borders.rationale: The doctrine is built on defending and extending borders and sovereignty; open borders contradict it.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; settlement expansion implies growth over limits.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technology is not a theme of the territorial doctrine, so adherents are split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power policy is outside the doctrine; none of the sources raise it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mainstream adherents work through the Knesset and settlement; the Jewish Underground splinter is a fringe, not typical.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist populism leans against it.

central-planning.rationale: Not stated; Likud strand is market-leaning and the planning left of the 1967 movement is a minority.

socialized-markets.rationale: Labor-kibbutz members were in the movement but modern carriers differ; not an issue for the doctrine.

land-value-tax.rationale: A land-value tax is not discussed by the doctrine or its sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance tax is not discussed by the doctrine or its sources.

basic-income.rationale: A basic income is not discussed by the doctrine or its sources.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tariff policy is not part of the territorial doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not stated, though state-sponsored settlement funding (as under Shamir) is a form of directed investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Agrarian settlement ideals feature in Zionism, but no stated property distribution doctrine here.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A state-sovereignty nationalism with no anti-money strand; its adherents are mainstream in economics.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream nationalist-right economics.

one-party-rule.rationale: Adherents compete in Knesset elections and the Likud platform speaks of government and negotiation, not single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; Israel is a republic and adherents work within it.

democracy-best.rationale: Jabotinsky called democracy sacred, and Likud works through elections, but the question of Palestinian voters in the territories strains the commitment.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums are not part of the doctrine, though the settler right has at times urged votes on territory.

workers-councils.rationale: The platform assumes parliamentary sovereignty of the Israeli state; councils play no role.

right-to-secede.rationale: The doctrine insists on Israeli sovereignty over the whole area; a secession right for regions is not considered.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents deny it in a democratic Israel, though a religious strand sees rabbinical authority.

political-violence-never.rationale: Jabotinsky justified force behind an iron wall and some splinters (Jewish Underground) used violence, but mainstream adherents claim legitimate defence.

war-builds-character.rationale: The sources present force as defensive necessity, not as character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: The religious strand bases the land claim on the Torah and sees redemption in settlement; Revisionists were mostly secular, so only mild disagreement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Gush Emunim is called theocratic, but secular Revisionist adherents reject halakhic law; genuinely split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state's armed control over territory is central; privatised defense contradicts it.

military-superiority.rationale: Jabotinsky's Iron Wall idea rests on overwhelming force making Arab resistance hopeless, and holding the territories depends on it.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The aim is a Jewish state in the whole land; it is primarily national-religious, so only partly ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Jabotinsky's nationalism and the Likud text frame history as national conflict, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equality of outcomes is not addressed; the doctrine concerns territory and sovereignty.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Palestinian claims to authority over their land are denied by the platform's sovereignty over the whole land, while Jews are seen as the land's historic people.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents reject the colonial label for Zionism; reparations for colonialism are not their issue and are opposed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; adherents emphasise Jewish national sovereignty, not unions of nations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Personal self-interest as a moral good is not addressed; the doctrine is communal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Settlement and defense are presented as national duties; no general doctrine.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nature's intrinsic value is not part of the doctrine, which values the land for national and religious reasons.

limit-population.rationale: The platform urges young Israelis and diaspora Jews to settle the land, so it is population-building.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pace of technological change is not part of the doctrine.

human-enhancement.rationale: Human enhancement is not an issue the doctrine addresses.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Algorithmic government is not an issue the doctrine addresses.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Security-first stance against terror organisations suggests distrust of state-blind encryption; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Religious strand sees return to biblical land as redemption, but this is a forward-looking settlement project.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The platform's land claim is explicitly principled and not to be traded for results.

direct-action.rationale: Gush Emunim's settling of land without prior consent as "facts on the ground" is direct action, but electoral politics are used too.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources show no commitment either way; Jabotinsky argues force is needed whatever the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No tradition of this; adherents are modernising nationalists.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: No such tradition in the doctrine.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; Labor kibbutz figures once favoured it but they are not the typical adherent now.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for use versus profit is not a topic of the doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Jabotinsky and Likud treat national conflict, not class exploitation, as the central question.

collective-farming.rationale: Labor-kibbutz participants in the 1967 movement favoured it, while Likud-Revisionists did not.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not part of the nationalist analysis, which sees Arab opposition to Zionism as the source of conflict.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation as theft is not a stated position; adherents fund settlement through the state.

harm-principle.rationale: A harm principle is not a stated position of the doctrine.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Group rights of the Jewish people to the land are the doctrine's core.

conscription.rationale: Israel conscripts; adherents back military service, though some Hardal circles resist parts of it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The right of exit versus voting is not a theme here.

state-as-business.rationale: Running government as a business is not part of the doctrine.

positive-liberty.rationale: Positive liberty is not a theme of the doctrine.

media-academia-power.rationale: Right-wing Israeli nationalists commonly say elites in media and universities oppose settlement, but this is not in the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; the claim rests on divine promise and history, not race science.

organic-representation.rationale: Guild or family representation is not part of the doctrine, which assumes the Knesset.

total-state.rationale: Adherents work within a parliamentary state and the platform proposes no total control.

national-rebirth.rationale: Greater Israel is part of Zionism's national revival; religious Zionists see retrieving the land as redemption.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Greater Israel is an irredentist idea of historic or desired borders, though the narrow variant seeks to keep 1967 gains rather than conquer more.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology of power is not an issue the doctrine takes up.

universal-morality.rationale: Religious strand sees a universal Torah morality, but it is not defined by the doctrine.

single-common-good.rationale: A single common good is not a stated position; the doctrine is a territorial claim.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Likud platform calls the Jewish right to the land of Israel eternal and indisputable, the premise of Greater Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The platform calls on Israeli youth and diaspora Jews to settle and cultivate the land throughout Eretz Israel.

revive-national-language.rationale: Hebrew revival is part of Zionism generally but is not specific to this doctrine.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workplace democracy is not part of the doctrine, and its adherents are split.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; religious schooling interests lean toward it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is outside the doctrine; carriers disagree.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link between political and economic freedom is not a theme of the doctrine.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule by moral example is not a position stated in the sources.

national-self-determination.rationale: Adherents affirm it for Jews, but deny it to Palestinians in the territories, so only partly literal.

force-without-un.rationale: The Iron Wall rests on Jewish power not awaiting consent, and the platform rejects imposed outside solutions.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The religious strand grounds the land claim in divine promise.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility of immigrants is not addressed; the sources are about territory.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare work requirements are not addressed by the doctrine.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalist doctrine favours national unity over class struggle; not directly stated.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; heritage, including the biblical homeland, is its basis.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; adherents align with the West, especially the US.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Religious strand favours it, secular does not.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest bans are not a position of the doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Platform text says not to dispossess anyone, and Jabotinsky promised equal rights for Arabs eventually; no racial classification doctrine.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil fuel policy is outside the doctrine.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; Jewish diaspora immigration is encouraged but its cultural terms are unspecified.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement narratives are not part of the doctrine's sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system is not a doctrinal matter, and Israel's list system is accepted by adherents.

national-mission.rationale: Religious-Zionist view of a redemptive role is a mission of redemption, not spreading a government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The question of structural patriarchy is not addressed in the sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed; the movement itself has had ministerial power.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not part of the doctrine; no source supports it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Adherents generally defend the army and security services against accountability claims over the territories.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A minimal state is not stated; settlement is state-supported.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Religious strand discourages intermarriage, but through religion, not race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Jabotinsky promised equal rights for Arabs once agreement is reached, but the doctrine subordinates Palestinians' political claims.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Jabotinsky openly described Zionism as colonisation, but adherents reject the label for a return to the ancestral homeland and the idea of displacement.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; religious-Zionist views on conversion are contested.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter is not a theme of the doctrine.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The religious-Zionist strand supports state-religious schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist question has no counterpart in the doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Jabotinsky says Arab consent will not come and colonisation proceeds regardless; yet adherents govern by Knesset elections.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance is not a theme of the doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Meir Kahane's Kach advocated transfer but Gush Emunim rejected it, so the mainstream says no.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Jabotinsky says colonisation proceeds regardless of consent under armed protection; adherents frame force as defensive.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition as the engine of progress is not stated by the doctrine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have themselves faced bans (Kach).

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept of freedom is not part of the doctrine.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split on the courts.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Priority to the poor is not a stated position of the doctrine.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a British issue outside the doctrine.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law is outside the doctrine, and Likud, religious and Labor-origin adherents differ.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The cause of poverty is not addressed in the sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Concern that absorbing Palestinians would end Jewish character (Begin avoided annexation for that reason) implies it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are not discussed; adherents differ over security measures.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not a theme of the doctrine.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed; adherents compete in a free press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; the army is a state body.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation waiting periods are not addressed; the doctrine speaks of Jewish return.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of legislators is not addressed by the doctrine.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Knesset parties that carry the idea vary in discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The platform insists on undivided Israeli sovereignty and no foreign administration, so pooling sovereignty is contrary to it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Command of the armed forces is not a doctrinal issue.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to Judaism; no stated position.

clerical-rule.rationale: Hardal rabbis exert influence, but the Likud and Revisionist mainstream rejects rabbinical rule.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship of art for moral reasons is not addressed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not addressed by the doctrine.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not addressed by the doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents rely on alliance with the US for security; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Settler civilian armed defence exists but the state army is the doctrine's instrument; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The platform praises settlement and cultivation of the land as redemptive, which suggests a pastoral ideal.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Educated elites as out of touch is not a stated position in the sources.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The religious strand holds the Jewish people uniquely chosen.

death-penalty.rationale: Right-wing nationalist adherents commonly favour death penalty for terrorists, though not stated in these sources.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Religious strand opposes it; no direct source.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Religious strand favours restriction; no direct source.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Aliyah and diaspora return imply descent-based belonging.

minority-language-support.rationale: The doctrine's focus is Jewish national character; not addressed directly.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions are not addressed, and religious and secular adherents differ.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nonconformity as a good is not addressed by the doctrine.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt cancellation is not addressed by the doctrine.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: This anti-colonial question has no counterpart in the doctrine.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-writing procedure is not addressed; Israel lacks a single constitution but adherents do not push this.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Trading freedom for growth is not addressed by the doctrine.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties are not addressed by the doctrine.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Security self-reliance and no outside-imposed solutions suggest support, though sources do not mention it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential elections are not addressed by the doctrine.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank independence is not addressed by the doctrine.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The 1977 Likud platform says Judea and Samaria will not pass to any foreign administration and sovereignty will hold between the sea and the Jordan.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The justification of property is not addressed by the doctrine.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental precaution is not addressed by the doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: Adherents value the US alliance, but this is not an explicit stance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Adherents deny the West Bank is occupied territory, claiming sovereignty over Judea and Samaria; annexation proposals appear from Likud and Rivlin.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religious strand opposes it; Revisionists are mixed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state's partisanship is not addressed by the doctrine.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Insistence on indivisible sovereignty suggests support for keeping territory by force, but the case is not discussed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Greater Israel claims sovereignty, not autonomy; limited autonomy for Palestinians is a Begin-era idea only.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax rate structure is not addressed by the doctrine.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is not addressed by the doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is not part of the doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional mixing is not addressed by the doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader veneration is not a stated element, though adherents honour figures like Jabotinsky.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is outside the doctrine, and religious and secular adherents differ.

land-redistribution.rationale: Jabotinsky speaks of land for those who lack it in Palestine, but adherents do not seek to redistribute estates; the issue is peripheral.

refugee-return.rationale: The platform sees land as Jewish and rejects a Palestinian state; return of refugees is unstated and inferred as opposed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The claim rests on biblical promise and historic homeland, not presence of co-nationals alone.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing apostasy is not addressed by the doctrine and is generally rejected in Israeli law.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress mandates are not part of the doctrine.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not addressed by the doctrine.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Union of kin peoples is not addressed by the doctrine.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Likud platform assumes unitary Israeli sovereignty over all the land.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Zionism and the platform call diaspora Jews to settle in Eretz Israel, opposing a diaspora-rights strategy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalist and religious accounts of history are not materialist.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust policy is not addressed by the doctrine.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not addressed by the doctrine.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The settler right criticises the Supreme Court as blocking settlement, but it is not stated in the sources.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not addressed by the doctrine.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade standards are not addressed by the doctrine.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral incentives are a socialist topic not addressed by the doctrine.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Gush Emunim's Jewish Underground did this, but most adherents were opposed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary titles are not an issue in the doctrine.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not a stated Greater Israel argument; Jabotinsky rejects the idea of paternalistic benefits as motivating Arabs.

patriotic-education.rationale: National revival is central; the platform calls for devotion to settlement of the land.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are not addressed by the doctrine.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not addressed by the doctrine.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalist crisis theory is not addressed by the doctrine.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Influence in former imperial regions is not addressed, apart from wider claims to biblical territory.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Freedom of association over discrimination law is not addressed by the doctrine.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed; Israel has no single constitution.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era treaties are not addressed, though adherents dispute Mandate-era partitions of the land.

elective-rulers.rationale: Adherents work in an elected parliament.

minority-veto.rationale: Contradicts national sovereignty and majority decision.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The right to resist rulers is not addressed, and the Jewish Underground shows a fringe tendency.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Adherents govern through the Knesset; not stated for this doctrine.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not addressed by the doctrine.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed by the doctrine.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Elite duties toward the poor are not addressed by the doctrine.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The doctrine is intensely activist; the Gush Emunim movement settled territory.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of mass culture is not addressed by the doctrine.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is not addressed by the doctrine.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving public office for native-born citizens is not addressed; Israel's founders were immigrants.

party-own-road.rationale: This communist-party question has no counterpart in the doctrine.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed by the doctrine.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Wider variants claim territory beyond 1967 on historical or biblical grounds, though narrow ones focus on holding what Israel already controls.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism in constitutions is not addressed by the doctrine.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; anti-communist nationalists commonly agree.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is not part of the doctrine.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist right generally agrees.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Male disadvantage is not addressed by the doctrine.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not addressed by the doctrine.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Institutional relativism is not addressed by the doctrine.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; army has influence over territorial policy but not constitutional guardianship.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paid domestic work is not addressed by the doctrine.

filial-duty.rationale: Religious tradition favours it; no direct source.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service examinations are not addressed by the doctrine.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Blocking foreign takeovers is not addressed by the doctrine.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Religious strand favours rabbinic divorce rules.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Recall of delegates is not addressed by the doctrine, which works through ordinary parliament.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed by the doctrine.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The doctrine treats the land as the Jewish people's, but without a tenure-by-use doctrine.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Adherents work through the Knesset; not stated.

single-official-language.rationale: Official language policy is not addressed beyond Hebrew revival in Zionism generally.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Sovereignty and Jewish settlement imply wanting land kept in Jewish hands, but it is not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate impact doctrine is not addressed by the doctrine.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not addressed by the doctrine.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Arming insurgents is not addressed by the doctrine.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervening in allied states is not addressed by the doctrine.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Israeli right backs limits on foreign NGO funding, but not in these sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Settling the land with Jews implies encouraging population growth.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; settlement by Jews anywhere is the aim.

job-guarantee.rationale: Job guarantees are not addressed by the doctrine.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not addressed by the doctrine.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; settler civil disobedience exists in fringe forms.

non-intervention.rationale: Adherents reject outside interference in settlement but not explicitly all intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed by the doctrine.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities are not part of the doctrine's sources.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Religious strand regards marriage as a religious institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Access to government information is not addressed by the doctrine.

local-production.rationale: Local production is not addressed by the doctrine.

informal-organisation.rationale: Informal anarchist organisation is not addressed, though Gush Emunim began as a grassroots movement.

religious-nation.rationale: Religious Zionists link the nation and land to the Torah, but secular Zionists define Jewishness nationally.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary deference is not addressed by the doctrine.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional revenue sharing is not addressed by the doctrine.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Likud was anti-Soviet.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery is not addressed by the doctrine.

religion-illusion.rationale: The religious strand sees divine promise and redemption in the land.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The historical role of capitalism is not addressed by the doctrine.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economics of women's equality is not addressed by the doctrine.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare is not addressed by the doctrine.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not addressed apart from Hebrew revival in Zionism generally.

treaties-binding.rationale: Adherents deny a binding territorial settlement of land claims to a minority within borders.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Labor kibbutz strand in the 1967 movement; most adherents do not hold this.

majority-settlement.rationale: The 1977 platform calls Jewish settlement throughout the Land of Israel the focal point of the Zionist effort, including areas with Arab populations.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A third economic way is not addressed by the doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; adherents are integrated with the world economy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: National revival and attachment to the biblical land imply Jewish history at the centre of schooling; not directly stated.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Common ownership of production is not addressed by the doctrine.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Some wider variants treat Mandate Palestine, including Transjordan, as one unit divided by outside powers, though mainstream adherents focus on the land west of the Jordan.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Soviet class character is not a question the doctrine considers.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The platform insists on sovereignty over all land with no solution imposed from outside, which favours Israel resisting international legal claims over the territories.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Likud platform calls the Jewish right to the land eternal and indisputable, and religious adherents ground it in the Torah promise.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Zionism of every strand treats the Holocaust as settled history and a justification for Jewish sovereignty; inferred from that, as the sources do not discuss denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The religious settler wing is socially conservative but the Revisionist and Likud tradition is liberal-nationalist and has not sought criminalisation; inferred, contested.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Revisionist and Likud politics operate within parliamentary democracy and oppose suppression of rivals; inferred from that tradition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Even Gush Emunim's religious vision works through a state with democratic law, and the secular Revisionist wing opposes religious coercion; inferred, contested.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The doctrine claims a national homeland to be settled and held, not overseas territory run for a metropole's profit; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A Muslim duty of armed resistance would apply to resisting Israeli control, so adherents would reject it; the topic is outside the doctrine, so inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Gush Emunim's theology accepted the secular state's sovereignty as a stage of redemption, so forcible removal of non-religious rulers is not its program; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The doctrine is territorial; settler movements are grassroots but Likud is hierarchical, so adherents are split on direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not a framework the nationalist right uses; inferred from its focus on national and security questions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Religious adherents oppose it and the secular right is mostly indifferent; inferred from that social-conservative lean.

assisted-dying.rationale: The religious wing opposes it on Jewish-law grounds, while secular Revisionists have no doctrine; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Revisionist and Likud politics define themselves as the national right against labour Zionism; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: The claim is a Marxist one; Revisionist and religious carriers did not frame work this way, and the Likud platform favours private enterprise, so this is inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Carriers focus on Arab claims to the land and security rather than Western cultural compatibility; adherents are split and the sources do not say.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Gush Emunim and religious adherents ground the claim in the divine promise of the land, while secular Revisionists argue from national right, so the strand leans toward yes.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious settlers wear religious dress publicly and the Israeli right opposes limiting it; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The doctrine does not address workplace law; adherents are split and this is inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Likud platform of 1977 mixes free enterprise with social aims, but economics is outside the doctrine; adherents are split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Revisionist Iron Wall doctrine holds that a strong military is the basis of the national project and the Likud platform stresses security.

rich-first.rationale: Economic development is not a doctrine of the strand and carriers are split between market-first and settlement-first views; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Likud tradition seeks strategic alliance with the West and the United States; Israel's nonalignment is not a stated aim; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Likud platform and the Revisionist tradition are committed to a parliamentary democracy in Israel; hereditary succession is alien to it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Likud's 1977 platform favours free enterprise; user-owned credit banks are not part of the doctrine, so this is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The doctrine is about territory and security, not lenders; adherents are split and this is inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Revisionist Zionism and the Likud platform assume universal suffrage in a democratic state.

domination-women-nature.rationale: A feminist-ecological critique not found in the Greater Israel sources; inferred disagreement from the right-wing, settlement-oriented outlook.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept; Likud's free-enterprise platform points to rejection, but the sources do not discuss it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Israeli right more often complains of a left-leaning media than of rich owners; inferred from the platform's free-enterprise stance.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Likud platform commits to the rule of law and the Knesset, though Gush Emunim ranked divine law above the state; majority view positive.

racial-franchise.rationale: Jabotinsky and the Likud platform affirm equal civil rights for all citizens, Arab and Jewish, in the state, while the Kach strand is excluded by scope.

online-participation.rationale: The doctrine does not address internet participation; adherents have no shared view and this is inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no common line and this is inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Israel's religious-law marriage system bars civil intermarriage, and religious-Zionist settlers (Gush Emunim) defend it; secular Likud voters are less keen.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The mainstream strand does not sponsor boycotts of Arab shops, which belong to fringe groups such as Kach; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The strand emphasises the Knesset and referendum-averse leadership on territory; inferred disagreement.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Gush Emunim followers read the Torah promise of the land as binding rather than reinterpretable; secular Likud voters are indifferent, so inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Greater Israel is a territorial doctrine; adherents span free-market Likud supporters and religious parties favouring the welfare state, so they are split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred: Israel has allowed open service since the 1990s and secular Likud supporters accept it, while the religious-Zionist settler strand objects, so adherents are split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: the Likud platform and Gush Emunim ground the land claim in Jewish tradition and the Torah promise, so state promotion of unbelief contradicts the doctrine.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the Iron Wall doctrine rests on force and security, and adherents want a strong state apparatus, so abolishing police and prisons is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: the Likud platform rejects a Palestinian state and asserts Jewish sovereignty over the land, so guaranteed communal shares of executive power are not favoured.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine has no welfare position, and adherents range from Likud free-marketeers to religious parties that support state aid alongside communal charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: term limits are not part of the doctrine, and adherent parties have had long-serving leaders without a settled view.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: the movement works through parliamentary politics and settlement activism and has no connection to delegable voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: adherents stress Israel's own security and survival, but the doctrine does not address global extinction risk, so views are split.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the religious-Zionist strand of Gush Emunim follows Orthodox practice, which reserves rabbinic office to men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: secular Revisionist adherents accept equal spouses while Orthodox religious settlers hold traditional roles, so the strand is split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the claim to exclusive national sovereignty over the land; the doctrine does not address resident foreigners directly.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; adherents span free-market Likud and religious-welfare positions.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the Likud platform's commitment to private enterprise.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the Revisionist Betar tradition of drilled, uniformed youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the security emphasis on deterrence and strength.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; self-reliance fits the Iron Wall, but alliances with great powers are accepted.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the Jewish-national focus on memory of the Holocaust.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between Labor-Zionist and free-market traditions.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Iron Wall argues the land can be held only by force that the Arab population cannot overcome, so defensive killing is accepted.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Likud platform calls the Jewish right to the land eternal and rooted in ancient history.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from religious-Zionist traditionalism.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from religious-Zionist family traditionalism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the settler movement's honouring of those killed for the land.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Gush Emunim saw settlement as redemptive while secular Revisionists argued from security; adherents split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Revisionism rejected a mere cultural centre and demanded a sovereign state holding the whole land to gather the Jewish people.

culture-before-state.rationale: Jabotinsky and Begin put political sovereignty and territory first.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from Orthodox religious Zionism, which treats the Torah as authoritative.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the Likud platform's liberal market stance, which does not call for ethnic economic control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the aim of holding the whole land as a single Israeli territorial unit.

missingStatements.text: A people's historical or religious tie to a land gives it a stronger claim than the claims of other peoples now living there.
missingStatements.rationale: The Likud platform calls the Jewish right to the land eternal and indisputable, and religious adherents ground it in the Torah promise.

missingStatements.text: Settling a particular land is a religious duty that helps bring redemption.
missingStatements.rationale: Gush Emunim, following the Kooks, held settlement of the captured territories to hasten messianic redemption.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to messianic religious Zionism; the statements already capture the land and security claims (no-land-for-peace, jewish-state-israel).

missingStatements.text: A state may keep captured territory permanently when its former borders are judged indefensible.
missingStatements.rationale: Gush Emunim viewed the pre-1967 borders as indefensible and sought to hold the territories through facts on the ground.

notes: Mainstream versions answer the democracy and equal-rights questions with strain, because annexing the West Bank raises the question of Palestinian citizenship; Begin avoided annexation partly for that reason. Wider Nile-to-Euphrates and Transjordan readings, and Kahanist transfer, would answer territorial-expansion and population-transfer more strongly.
